title: `fsum`, `kahan_sum`, `sumkahan` and `favg` of an infinity and finite values: NaN at 2.0.0, the infinity at 2.0.1
verdict: `fsum` and `favg` (also `kahan_sum`, `sumkahan`) of one kind of infinity with finite values give that infinity at 2.0.1, grouped and over a window; at 2.0.0 they gave NaN once a finite value followed the infinity; both infinities still give NaN
description: The observation `sum-avg-infinities` (`engines/duckdb/replay/probes.json`) over a table of 9 rows: `fsum` and `favg` of a group of `+inf` and `1.0` give NaN at 2.0.0 and `inf` at 2.0.1; of `-inf` and `1.0`, NaN and `-inf`; the window frames `w1` to `w7` the same. `sum` and `avg` are unchanged (the infinity at both versions), `+inf` with `-inf` still gives NaN at every function, and finite groups are unchanged.

These are DuckDB's own functions, which sverify reaches only as black boxes (`python/src/sverify/black_box.py`, `engines/duckdb/Sverify/DuckDB/Boxes.lean`): their only law is `nonNull`, which a NaN and an infinity both meet, so no theorem about a plan that calls them changes, and no profile row reads them. The model's `AggFn.fsum` is not this function: it is written as DuckDB's `SUM`, which the probe shows unchanged. It supersedes the infinite-input claim of `duckdb-kahan-sum` (true at 2.0.0).
reference: A black box is the engine's own function; Lean has no evaluator for an aggregate black box (`evalAgg` is `unevaluated`).
